nodes.name: DeepWalk
nodes.note: Treats short random walks over a graph as “sentences” and feeds them to word2vec's SkipGram — nodes that co-occur in walks end up close in embedding space. Structure-only and transductive, but the paper nearly every later embedding method positions itself against.

nodes.name: node2vec
nodes.note: Adds two bias parameters, p and q, to DeepWalk's random walk so it can lean toward local community structure or broader structural roles. Same embed-then-classify pipeline, now tunable to the task.

nodes.name: GCN
nodes.note: Collapses spectral graph convolutions into a first-order approximation: average neighbor features, multiply by a weight matrix, activate. Uses both structure and features, trains in seconds, and became the template every message-passing GNN builds on.

nodes.name: GraphSAGE
nodes.note: Replaces a per-node embedding lookup with a learned aggregation function over local neighborhoods, so embeddings can be computed for nodes never seen during training — the paper that made graph learning inductive.

nodes.name: GAT
nodes.authors: Veličković, Cucurull, Casanova, Romero, Liò, Bengio
nodes.note: Learns attention weights over a node's neighbors instead of averaging them equally, so the model decides which neighbors matter most — bringing learned weighting into message passing.

nodes.name: GIN
nodes.note: Proves that sum aggregation with an MLP is exactly as powerful as the 1-Weisfeiler-Lehman test — the theoretical ceiling for message-passing GNNs. Turns “which aggregator should I use” into a provable question.

nodes.name: PNA
nodes.note: Shows that any single aggregator (mean, sum, max…) loses information a real-valued neighborhood can carry, and combines several aggregators scaled by node degree instead. One aggregator isn't enough.

nodes.name: GATv2
nodes.note: Finds that GAT's attention is “static” — the ranking of neighbors doesn't actually depend on the query node — and fixes it with a one-line reordering of the attention computation. A small change with an outsized effect.

nodes.name: DGN
nodes.authors: Beaini, Passaro, Létourneau, Hamilton, Corso, Liò
nodes.note: Borrows directionality from CNN kernels: computes gradient fields from the graph Laplacian's eigenvectors so a layer can tell “this way” from “that way” instead of treating every neighbor as unordered.

nodes.name: Graphormer
nodes.authors: Ying, Cai, Luo, Zheng, Ke, He, Shen, Liu
nodes.note: Injects graph structure directly into a standard Transformer's attention via three bias terms (centrality, spatial, edge) rather than constraining attention or hand-crafting positional features. Beat every GNN on the largest graph-level benchmark available at the time.
